notes:
Three checks that claimed more than they checked.

**Click depth is no longer reported from a link graph Docket never saw.**
`supports_link_graph_claims` governs "inlink counts, orphan status and click
depth" by its own definition, and two of those three consulted it. On a site
whose navigation is built by JavaScript, the same check withheld its orphan
answer as untrustworthy and printed its depth answer from the identical
unreadable graph — with advice attached that sends you restructuring your
navigation. It now withholds and says so, because silence would read as "no
deep pages".

**Session IDs are matched as parameters, not as three letters anywhere.**
`?rsid=12` is an analytics report suite id and was reported as a session ID at
HIGH severity, with a warning about an infinite duplicate-content space. And
`/shop/item;jsessionid=9F3A2B` — the canonical Java form — was not seen at all,
because only the query string was read.

**hreflang region codes are checked against IANA's registry.** The finding said
"the country must be a real ISO 3166-1 code" while checking a three-entry typo
table, so `en-XX` passed. Codes in ISO 3166-1's private-use ranges can never be
a country and are now reported; codes merely absent from the table are a notice
rather than a defect, because the table has a date. `en-un` is reported too:
Google documents that EU, UN and UK have no effect in an hreflang annotation.
